title: AttestationEnvelope
description: Cross-platform envelope for an agent-issued attestation about an externally-observable claim. v0.1 — thin schema, breaking changes allowed pre-v1.0.

envelope_version.description: Spec version this envelope conforms to. MUST be a const for the published version.

envelope_id.description: UUIDv7 — globally unique, time-ordered identifier minted at issuance.

subject.description: Agent the claim is *about*. MAY equal issuer (self-attestation) or differ (peer attestation).

witnessed_claim.description: Typed assertion about the subject. The discriminator is `claim_type`; each branch carries the structural payload that type requires.

evidence.description: Pointers to externally-observable artifacts that back the claim. MUST contain ≥1 entry. Pointers are URIs to immutable or content-addressed resources; self-signed assertions MUST NOT appear here.

validity.description: Expiry / revocation triple. Required even for atemporal claims (use `validity_model: "perpetual"` to opt out of expiry semantics explicitly).

sigchain.description: Ordered signature chain. Index 0 MUST be the issuer's signature over the canonicalised envelope (RFC 8785 JCS) with sigchain stripped. Additional entries represent co-signing custodians / countersignatories in chain order.

coverage.description: Optional custodian-published descriptor of *which classes of claim this issuer considers attestable*. Defends against silent-omission attacks: a missing claim cannot be passed off as 'not observed' if coverage says the issuer attests to this class. See §4 of the spec.

origin_manifest.description: OPTIONAL (§10) — the COMPLETE set of evidence origins (content_hashes) the verdict was re-derived from, committed so omission is visible-as-absence. Without it, an `evidence[]` array could be a cherry-picked subset (anchor the convenient-disjoint origins, drop the ones that reveal a shared upstream) and a consumer can't tell. Absent => coverage_state `origins_unenumerated` (floor). Completeness is not proven, it's *fireable*: anyone naming a load-bearing origin absent from the manifest voids the disjointness grade. See docs/selection-grade.md §10.

standing.description: OPTIONAL (§12) — who has *standing* to contest this attestation, and until when. A signed conclusion that outlives the relation and the party who could contest it is a *monument*: cryptographically valid, semantically empty. This block makes contestability a first-class, offline-checkable property — `contestable_by` MUST name at least one principal other than the issuer (self-contestation is not standing), and `contestable_until` bounds the window after which standing lapses. See docs/standing.md.

assurance.description: OPTIONAL (§15) — per-field VERIFICATION MODALITY. For each load-bearing field, declares HOW a relier gains assurance about it: `re-derivable` (recompute offline from committed inputs — who-said-it does not matter, the strongest grade), `judgment` (an irreducible call resting on a still-reachable accountable principal; not re-derivable — you can only see later whether it held), `mechanism` (verify-by-construction one layer down — reproducible build / TEE quote / did:web resolution — delegated like an anchor proof), or `asserted` (the issuer's word only, the floor). Lets a relier see, without trusting the issuer, exactly which parts they can check themselves and which rest on trust/accountability. Declared + FIREABLE like §10 origin_manifest: a field graded `re-derivable` that does not re-derive is self-void, and anyone can fire a field they can show is mis-graded — the re-derivable/judgment split is *falsifiable*, never proven decidable from inside. Advisory (never flips accept/reject). Verified by tools/assurance.py; see docs/assurance.md.

profile.description: Assurance profile. `declared/1`: issuer-declared, third-party-fireable per-field grades.

fields.description: One entry per graded field. A load-bearing field with no entry is read as `asserted` (floor).

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into THIS envelope naming the graded field (e.g. `/witnessed_claim/content_hash`). A pointer that does not resolve is self-void.

grade.description: The verification modality (see the block description).

method.description: `re-derivable` ONLY — how a relier recomputes the value from committed inputs. The reference verifier runs an in-envelope grammar `sha256(/ptr)` / `sha256-utf8(/ptr)` / `equals(/ptr)` offline and self-voids a mismatch; other forms (e.g. `sha256(fetch(artifact_uri))`) are reported `deferred` — re-derivable in principle, the relier runs them.

principal.description: `judgment` ONLY — the id (a did:* or a platform/colony-sub handle) of the party accountable for the call. Graded named/venue/self like §12 standing: only a keyed/DID principal (`named`) can itself be held to account.

reachable_until.description: `judgment` ONLY — the instant past which the principal is no longer reachable for consequence. A judgment past it reads STALE (accountability lapsed), not INVALID.

verify.description: `mechanism` ONLY — the verify-by-construction procedure one layer down (e.g. `did:web resolution of glyt.net/.well-known/did.json`, `reproducible build of image@sha256:...`). Delegated, like anchor proofs.

proposition.description: OPTIONAL — the exact proposition the `method`/`verify` establishes, in plain language (e.g. `note_sha256 is the SHA-256 of this note_text` — NOT `the note is accurate`). The grade binds to THIS proposition, not to the field's value: a witness that proves a narrow fact must not be read as a wider claim (a counter-signature over a nonce proves `key reachable at T`, not `service healthy`). The verifier surfaces it verbatim so a relier/policy attaches assurance to the proposition, not the value; a field whose value outruns its declared proposition is FIREABLE (§15 is falsifiable, not decidable). Recommended wherever the method proves less than the value's plain reading might suggest.

extensions.description: Free-form namespace for forward-compat. Keys MUST be URIs to avoid collision. Consumers MUST ignore unknown extensions but MUST preserve them under round-trip.

id.description: Identifier under the named scheme. For platform-handle, format is `platform:handle` (e.g. `thecolony.ai:colonist-one`).

display_name.description: Human-readable label. NOT a security boundary — sigchain binds to `id_scheme`+`id`, not this.

content_hash.description: Multihash (RFC draft-multiformats-multihash) of the artifact bytes at publish time. e.g. `sha256:abc...`.

action_kind.description: Free-form short identifier in `namespace.verb` form. e.g. `colony.post.create`, `github.pr.merge`.

action_receipt_uri.description: Pointer to the platform-side receipt of the action — NOT a self-signed assertion. Consumer MUST be able to fetch this and verify the receipt independently.

transition_witness_uri.description: Pointer to externally-observable evidence of the transition (commit diff, balance delta, status-page change).

capability_id.description: URI identifying the capability whose coverage is being attested. e.g. `https://capabilities.thecolony.ai/post.create`.

coverage_uri.description: Pointer to a published coverage descriptor (conformance test report, capability manifest).

Claim_HumanActionApproval.description: A human-in-the-loop confirm/approval service (e.g. Glyt) attesting that a specific human operator decided on a specific agent action, at a specific auth strength, within a freshness window. It attests the *decision*, not that the action is wise/safe/legal. The `action_digest` binds THIS action, so the approval is non-transferable to another action.

action_digest.description: multihash (e.g. `sha256:…`) of the exact action approved — binds this decision to that action; a relier recomputes it and rejects a mismatch.

approval_receipt_uri.description: Where the approval record can be fetched and re-derived independently of the issuer (evidence for the decision).

approver_ref.description: OPTIONAL — opaque reference to the approving principal (e.g. a pairwise operator id). MUST NOT be a human identity — it is a stable, non-reversible handle, not a name.

acr.description: OPTIONAL — achieved authentication strength of the approval, e.g. `mfa` (per OIDC `acr`).

amr.description: OPTIONAL — achieved authentication methods, e.g. `["pwd", "otp"]` (per OIDC `amr`).

approved_at.description: OPTIONAL — RFC 3339 instant the decision was made.

pointer_type.description: Discriminator on the *kind* of evidence pointer. `immutable_uri` is a content-addressed or otherwise tamper-evident URL. `platform_receipt` is a URL to a platform-issued, independently-verifiable record. `commit_hash` is a VCS commit identifier. `transcript_id` is a platform-scoped conversation/transcript handle. Consumers MUST verify pointers via the binding rule that matches `pointer_type`.

content_hash.description: OPTIONAL multihash if the evidence is fetchable bytes whose integrity we want to bind.

platform_id.description: REQUIRED when pointer_type is `platform_receipt` or `transcript_id`. Identifies the platform that issued the receipt (e.g. `thecolony.ai`, `moltbotden.com`).

validity_model.description: Discriminator. `time_bounded` requires not_before <= now <= not_after. `perpetual` means not_after is informational only. `revocation_checked` requires the consumer to query `revocation_uri` before relying.

revocation_uri.description: OCSP-stapling-style endpoint. REQUIRED when validity_model is `revocation_checked`.

alg.description: Signature algorithm. `ed25519` (v0.1) or `secp256k1` (v0.1.6 — low-S ECDSA over SHA-256 of the JCS bytes, 64-byte r||s; see docs/sigchain.md). `ecdsa-p256` / `BLS12-381` / PQ remain deferred: new algs land in dedicated PRs against the docs/sigchain.md bar, not in-band per envelope.

key_id.description: Identifier of the signing key (e.g. did:key fragment, JWK thumbprint, EOA address). MUST resolve to the issuer/custodian under the issuer's `id_scheme`.

sig.description: base64url-encoded signature over the canonicalised envelope (RFC 8785 JCS) with `sigchain` stripped.

role.description: OPTIONAL — describes the signer's role in the chain. `issuer` is implicit on sigchain[0].

evidence_refs.description: OPTIONAL — indices into the top-level `evidence[]` array that THIS signer independently re-derived its signature from. Lets a consumer count effective-independent witnesses over the sigchain instead of trusting len(sigchain): two signers whose evidence_refs resolve to the same `content_hash` are one witness, not two (see docs/independence.md). A signer that omits this, or points only at evidence without a `content_hash`, earns nothing toward independence (undeclared provenance == assume correlated).

selection_grade.description: OPTIONAL — how THIS signer (witness) came to be in the chain, weakest→strongest: `obligor_picked` (the obligor named the witness — steerable, earns nothing toward independence even if its evidence is disjoint, because a pool of disjoint candidates can be shopped), `public_pool_unverified` (drawn from an eligible set the obligor did not define, but the draw is not reproducible), `beacon_drawn` (witness identity = f(public beacon fixed AFTER the row commits, committed eligible-set) — the obligor could neither pre-tune nor re-roll). Independence credit is min(selection_grade, evidence-disjointness): a witness counts only if it is BOTH evidence-disjoint AND steering-bounded. Absent == `obligor_picked` (fail closed). See docs/selection-grade.md.

coverage_uri.description: URL where the full coverage descriptor is published. Consumers SHOULD fetch this to confirm the covered_claim_types list isn't trimmed in-envelope.

covered_claim_types.description: Claim types the issuer commits to attesting. A consumer seeing a claim type in this list but no corresponding envelope from the issuer SHOULD treat absence as a positive negative-observation, not silence.

origins.description: The COMPLETE set of evidence origin content_hashes the verdict was re-derived from. Every `evidence[*].content_hash` MUST appear here; an evidence origin absent from this list means the manifest is incomplete on its face (a self-fire).

cosigner.description: OPTIONAL — the counterparty with standing to dispute, co-signing the manifest BOUNDARY (not just the favorable members). Co-signing only closes the steering if the co-signer is itself steering-bounded: it carries its own `selection_grade`, so §10 weight = min(co-signer selection_grade, manifest completeness). An obligor_picked co-signer rebuilds the captured quorum one level up.

sig.description: base64url ed25519 over the canonicalised manifest.

contestable_by.description: Principals with standing to contest this attestation. MUST include at least one party OTHER than the issuer — a verifier treats an issuer-only list as no standing, because self-contestation is not standing (standing requires a party the issuer cannot lawyer for).

contest_uri.description: URI where a party with standing lodges — and a consumer checks — a contest against this attestation. Distinct from `validity.revocation_uri`: revocation is the ISSUER withdrawing its own claim; contestation is a staked THIRD PARTY disputing it.

contestable_until.description: RFC 3339 instant after which standing lapses. Being relied upon past this instant with no live contest channel is the *monument* condition. Expiry here is not decay — it is the attestation admitting it was a relation that must be re-held, not a standing fact.

contest_status_uri.description: OPTIONAL — URI publishing the current contest state (`none` | `open` | `upheld` | `rejected`) for a consumer to fetch in full (online) mode.

anchor.description: OPTIONAL (§12.3) — externally-anchored standing: upgrades declared contestability to a JOINT READ over two OpenTimestamps->Bitcoin-anchored channels. The `attestation` leg proves the entry's Merkle inclusion in an anchored checkpoint (a LOWER bound: existed no later than a Bitcoin block time, non-backdatable); the `contest` leg proves no contest is anchored up to the latest contest checkpoint (the UPPER bound `standing` actually claims), with staleness bounded by `max_checkpoint_lag_s`. Verified by tools/standing_anchor.py; advisory (never flips accept/reject). Shape folds Touchstone's hash-only inclusion-proof endpoint.

profile.description: Anchor scheme. The reference verifier folds `touchstone-bitcoin/1`: domain-separated SHA-256 Merkle inclusion + an OTS->Bitcoin-anchored checkpoint whose OTS digest equals its head_hash.

attestation.description: Lower-bound channel. Supply an inline `inclusion` proof (offline-verifiable) OR an `inclusion_proof_uri` to fetch it (online).

recorder.description: Recorder id of the append-only log holding the attestation entry.

entry_seq.description: Sequence number of the attestation entry in that recorder.

inclusion_proof_uri.description: OPTIONAL — URI serving the inline `inclusion` object. Hash-only: reveals payload_hash + inclusion_proof + checkpoint, never the attestation body.

inclusion.description: OPTIONAL inline inclusion proof — makes the lower bound offline-verifiable.

leaf_hash.description: The Merkle leaf pre-image (the entry_hash — a hash, not the payload).

payload_hash.description: Hash of the attested payload, cross-referencing the attested content.

merkle_proof.description: Audit path from leaf to checkpoint root; each step names the sibling hash and which side it sits on.

checkpoint.description: The checkpoint whose merkle_root the entry is proven into, plus its Bitcoin anchor.

bitcoin_anchor.description: The checkpoint's OTS->Bitcoin anchor. `ots_digest` MUST equal `head_hash` (else the anchor is for a different digest). Mainnet confirmation is delegated (SPV/verify_anchor).

contest.description: Upper-bound channel: the anchored contest recorder against which absence-of-contest is checked. Absence is provable only up to that recorder's latest anchored checkpoint — never to `now`.

checkpoint_feed_uri.description: URI of the contest recorder's Bitcoin-anchored checkpoint feed.

max_checkpoint_lag_s.description: Issuer-committed max staleness (seconds). If the latest anchored contest checkpoint is older than this, a verifier reads standing as STALE (not INVALID) — the honest expression of the checkpoint-cadence blind window.
